cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Brighter Side
cards.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No tickets sold! Perfect: I can finish teaching you to project before anyone hears our play.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The theatre has cancelled us. They want the stage cleared.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better. You're ready to win over people who haven't come to listen. We'll hire the pub upstairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They kept our deposit. All we can afford is the bus home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful, your first touring show! Start quietly at the back, like I taught you; by the next stop you'll have reached the whole bus.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 empty seats become time to teach projection; A3 venue loss becomes progress toward incidental audiences; A5 only bus fare becomes a touring milestone using taught audience reach.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 cancellation prompts A3 pub audience; B4 lost funds forces A5 bus audience, extending the already introduced incidental-listener challenge.

relationship.evidence: B4 states the real remaining option rather than supplying an artificial question.

heightening.evidence: A5 treats B4 narrow travel option as a larger performance achievement and gives a playable opening tactic.

specificity.evidence: A1 play/no tickets and B4 bus fare establish shrinking means; the audience reinterpretation follows those facts.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 first-touring-show is a character interpretation tied to actual movement, with a concrete quiet-to-whole-bus tactic.
